why: A => B: A's theorem_3_33 applied to the working form h.toContractionGerm of B's sc0-contraction germ gives the canonical solution germ sol of class sc^k on germ s; B's arbitrary solution representative delta equals sol near 0 by uniqueness of fixed points in O 0 (ContractionGerm.eq_sol, continuity of delta, delta(0)=0), so delta is sc^k on V' = V cap germ s cap {delta in O 0}. Glue: partial quadrant => quadrant-like, and sc^k of f = w - B(a,w) => sc^k of B (pairing with pr2 and the sc-operator (u,v) -> u - v). B => A fails for genuine generality: A allows any finite-dimensional P and any quadrant-like (convex, 0 in, nonempty interior) C~, and its main form only needs a 1/2-contraction on explicit regions (ContractionGerm), while B covers only R^n, partial quadrants and Definition 3.28's eps-contraction; A also pins the domain to the specific germs germ s.
